comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
## STOPPED — this needs a design decision, and I am not making it unilaterally

Picked up in a batch selected as "mechanical, no product judgement needed". It is not
mechanical, exactly as this ticket's own description warned ("Not a mechanical fix… That is a
judgement task about the 429 policy surface, not a find-and-replace"). Leaving it OPEN and
unclaimed. Below are the measured facts and the two competing options so whoever takes it can
decide from evidence rather than re-derive it.

### Measured on current origin/main

`_step0_names` sweeps 4 files. `adapters/jira/` actually holds **12** modules. The 8 unswept
non-`__init__` modules define **90** members in total:

    acli_subprocess.py 10   adf.py 32   backend.py 25   comment_limits.py  1
    jira_fields.py      2   outbound_fields.py 11   probe.py 5   rich_text_codec.py 4

Note the description's list of newly-in-scope modules was missing two: `acli_subprocess.py`
(which the module docstring itself names as one of the FOUR 429 behaviours — `_run_acli`'s
deliberate `_rate_limit_backoff` retry) and `jira_fields.py`.

The decisive number for the anti-drift variant: scanning all 8 unswept modules for members
whose name is already in `_CLASSIFIED_MUTATING` yields exactly **2 defs in 1 module** —
`backend.py::set_relationship` (:217) and `backend.py::add_comment` (:271). Those are precisely
the two the 8a5e disposition already measured as one-line pure delegations to
`self.transport.<same name>(...)`. Nothing else in the package collides.

### Option A — derive the file set (glob `adapters/jira/*.py`)

Satisfies AC1 literally and is drift-proof by construction: a new transport module is swept the
day it lands. Cost: `test_enumeration_completeness_every_step0_name_is_accounted_for` goes RED
against all 90 members, each of which must be individually classified as mutating or entered in
`_NON_MUTATING` with a recorded reason. That classification is a real 429-policy judgement, not
clerical — and it is the kind that fails quietly: mis-marking a member NON-MUTATING silently
removes it from a safety sweep, and nothing downstream catches it. It also changes what the
sweep *is*: today it is scoped to the TRANSPORT surface, and 8a5e's disposition concluded that
scoping is CORRECT. A glob over the package silently redefines the sweep's subject from
"transport" to "everything in the jira package", which is a scope decision, not a refactor.

### Option B — anti-drift assertion, keep the explicit list

Satisfies AC1's second branch. Keeps the sweep's transport scoping (the thing 8a5e ruled
correct) and fails the build when a module outside the list defines a `_CLASSIFIED_MUTATING`
name without being a pure delegating facade. Much smaller blast radius — it is green today
against 2 known-benign defs. Cost: it hinges entirely on defining "pure delegating facade"
programmatically, and THAT is the judgement. A one-line `return self.transport.x(...)` is easy;
a delegation with a guard, a retry, a log line, or an argument transform is not, and every
loosening of the predicate reopens the hole the assertion exists to close. It is also weaker
than A by design: it catches a *renamed-to-a-known-name* mutation, not a genuinely NEW mutating
member with a new name — which is the drift scenario the ticket's opening paragraph actually
describes ("a NEW transport module added beside those four would not be swept").

### The decision required

Neither option is obviously right, and they trade off against each other rather than dominating:
A is complete but demands 90 policy judgements and silently widens the sweep's subject;
B is cheap and preserves the transport scoping but only guards the narrower renamed-name case.
A third shape exists (glob restricted to a declared TRANSPORT module set, with an assertion that
the declaration itself stays complete) which arguably gets both properties, at the cost of a new
declaration to keep honest.

Whoever picks this up should choose deliberately and record the reason, since AC3's mutation
check ("a new transport module carrying an unswept mutating member turns the guard RED") is
satisfied by A but NOT by B as literally worded — so the choice also settles whether AC3 needs
rewording.

No code change made. Ticket left open and unclaimed.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
OPERATOR DECISION (2026-08-07): OPTION B — the anti-drift guard, not the glob.

The sweep's file list stays scoped to the transport layer as ticket 8a5e ruled correct. Add a guard that catches the drift case — a classified name being renamed or moved out from under the sweep — rather than widening the sweep's subject.

Rejected: the glob option. Measurement made the cost concrete: it pulls 90 new members across 8 modules into scope, each requiring individual mutating/non-mutating classification against the 429 policy, and it silently redefines what the sweep is ABOUT — from 'the transport layer' to 'the whole package' — contradicting 8a5e. That is a large classification effort in exchange for widening a boundary someone deliberately drew.

Supporting measurement for B being sufficient today: scanning all 8 unswept modules for names already in `_CLASSIFIED_MUTATING` yields exactly 2 defs in 1 module, both known-benign delegations. So B is green now and its job is to stay that way.

Consequence to handle in the same change: AC3 as literally worded is satisfied by the glob option but NOT by B. Rewrite AC3 to state what B actually guarantees — drift detection over the declared transport surface — rather than leaving a criterion that this decision cannot satisfy. (Per the operator's standing ruling: an unmeetable criterion is a defect in the criterion, to be remediated before close.)

Note the ticket's own scope section lists `scripts/canary_bridge.py` but omits `acli_subprocess.py` and `jira_fields.py`, the latter named by the test's own docstring as one of the four 429 behaviours. Reconcile that list while implementing.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
Implementation pushed as Gerrit change 1575 (option B, per the 2026-08-07 operator ruling).

What landed in `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_cloud_rate_limit_sweep_heldout.py` (no production code touched):

- `_SWEPT_TRANSPORT_MODULES` — the four transport paths are now a named constant consumed by `_step0_names()`, so the sweep's declared subject is a reviewable artifact rather than a literal buried in a helper. Still exactly four modules; no package-wide glob (AC1).
- `_unswept_jira_modules()` — DERIVES the guard's scope as the package listing minus the swept set minus `__init__.py`, so `acli_subprocess.py` and `jira_fields.py` (both missing from earlier hand-written scope notes) are covered, and a module added beside the four is covered the day it lands (AC2).
- `_is_pure_transport_facade()` — the AST predicate. Admits only `return self.transport.<same name>(args forwarded unchanged)`, optionally preceded by a docstring. Rejects extra statements, guards, retries, logging, argument transforms, dropped/reordered args, non-transport or renamed targets, `*args`/`**kwargs` passthrough, async defs, and no-return bodies. Scans at any nesting depth so a nested class cannot hide a mutation (AC3).
- `_KNOWN_BENIGN_COLLISIONS` — the accepted set is asserted to be EXACTLY `backend.py::set_relationship` and `backend.py::add_comment`; a new accepted facade is a deliberate 429-policy decision, not drift (AC4).
- 15 rejection fixtures plus one acceptance fixture (AC5). Mutation-checked against the real tree as well: appending a non-facade `add_comment` to `jira_fields.py` turns `test_antidrift_unswept_classified_collisions_are_only_pure_transport_facades` RED naming `jira_fields.py::add_comment`; reverting restores green.
- `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and the whole `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler` suite (2410 tests) pass (AC6).

On the AC3 rewording the operator required in the same change: it was already applied to the description by the EDIT event at 1786293886890275001, which replaced the original glob-only criterion with the option-B wording now in the ticket (current AC3 = the pure-facade acceptance rule; current AC5 = drift detection over the declared transport surface). Verified against the CREATE event's original text, so no further description edit was needed. Plan review PASSED with 0 blocking findings and was signed before claim.

compiled_state.description:
## Context

The Cloud rate-limit sweep intentionally covers four transport-surface modules under `adapters/jira/`. Its `_step0_names()` input is hardcoded, so a classified mutating method can be renamed or moved into an unswept sibling module without the completeness assertion noticing. A package-wide glob was evaluated and rejected because it would redefine the sweep from the transport surface to the entire Jira package and require policy classification of 90 unrelated members.

Current measurement finds exactly two definitions outside the swept modules whose names are in `_CLASSIFIED_MUTATING`: `backend.py::set_relationship` and `backend.py::add_comment`. Both are pure, same-name `self.transport` delegations. The unswept package set also includes `acli_subprocess.py` and `jira_fields.py`; neither currently collides with the classified mutating names.

## Operator decision

Implement option B: retain the explicit transport file list and add a strict anti-drift guard over every other Python module in `adapters/jira/`. A classified mutating name is allowed outside the sweep only when its body is a pure same-name transport delegation with unchanged arguments. Reject package-wide globbing.

## Plan

- Make the four swept transport paths an explicit named constant used by `_step0_names()`.
- Parse every other Jira adapter Python module with `ast` and identify functions whose names collide with `_CLASSIFIED_MUTATING`.
- Accept only the deliberately narrow facade shape already used by `backend.py`: one return statement calling `self.transport.<same_name>` with the declared arguments forwarded unchanged. Any guard, retry, logging, argument transform, extra statement, or non-transport target fails.
- Add a test proving the current two backend facades are the only accepted collisions and a mutation-style fixture proving an unswept non-facade `add_comment` turns the guard red.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The existing transport sweep remains scoped to the same four modules; no package-wide glob widens the 429 policy surface.
- [x] An anti-drift assertion scans every other `adapters/jira/*.py` module, including `acli_subprocess.py` and `jira_fields.py`, for names in `_CLASSIFIED_MUTATING`.
- [x] The only allowed collision shape is a pure same-name `self.transport` delegation with arguments forwarded unchanged.
- [x] The current `backend.py::set_relationship` and `backend.py::add_comment` facades pass the guard.
- [x] A new or moved unswept definition using a classified mutating name fails unless it is that exact pure-facade shape.
- [x] The focused Cloud rate-limit sweep passes without changing production code.

file_impact.reason: name the swept transport set, add AST anti-drift predicate, and prove unswept classified mutations fail unless they are exact transport facades
